facts.fact: Broadcast television accounted for 20.1% of total U.S. TV viewing time in May 2025, according to Nielsen's Gauge data.
facts.quote: Broadcast television accounts for 20.1% of total U.S. TV viewing time, according to [Nielsen's Gauge](https://www.nielsen.com/data-center/the-gauge/) data from May 2025.

facts.fact: Broadcast viewing declined 21% compared to May 2021, according to the article's reading of Nielsen Gauge data.
facts.quote: Broadcast viewing has declined 21% compared to May 2021, when Nielsen first launched The Gauge measurement system.

facts.fact: Streaming captured 44.8% of total TV viewing in May 2025, per Nielsen Gauge data cited in the article.
facts.quote: placing it behind both streaming (44.8%) and cable (24.1%) in terms of audience attention.

facts.fact: In May 2025, streaming viewership (44.8%) exceeded the combined broadcast and cable share (44.2%) for the first time.
facts.quote: For the first time ever, streaming viewership (44.8%) exceeded the combined viewing share of broadcast and cable (44.2%).

facts.fact: Streaming viewership increased 71% over the period from May 2021 to May 2025.
facts.quote: During that same period, streaming viewership increased by 71%, demonstrating a clear and accelerating shift

facts.fact: The big four broadcast networks (ABC, CBS, NBC, and FOX) together captured approximately 18% of total TV viewing in May 2025.

facts.fact: No individual broadcast network exceeded 5% of total TV viewing share in May 2025.

facts.fact: YouTube alone captured 12.5% of all television viewing in May 2025.

facts.fact: Broadcast's share of TV viewing rebounded to 23.2% in November 2025, which the article attributes largely to NFL coverage and fresh content.

facts.fact: The Super Bowl draws over 100 million viewers annually, per the article.
